title: Packing and covering in infinite matroids
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: OpenAI's theorem (2026) that in ZFC there are two self-dual matroids on a countable set whose ground set is not the union of an independent set of each, so the infinite matroid packing/covering conjecture of Bowler and Carmesin is false. The first lesson gives the axioms of Bruhn, Diestel, Kriesell, Pendavingh and Wollan, direct sums and a reduction to independent coverings. The second builds density ideals on a countable set cut into blocks, independent columns, an ultrafilter avoiding the larger ideal, an ordinal rank on its members and simultaneous reservations. The third defines probes inside one density class and proves interpolation and interval alternatives. The fourth assembles a self-dual uniform matroid by a transfinite recursion of length continuum. The fifth places copies along a double ray and derives an infinite descending sequence of ordinals.
prerequisites: core course Mathematical Logic, Set Theory, and Computability (C80): Button, Set Theory: An Open Introduction (Open Logic Project), Proposition 10.2, Theorem 11.4, Lemma 14.2, Corollary 14.10, Theorem 15.11, Proposition 15.12, Theorem 5.16, Theorem 16.6

open_obligations: Bowler-Carmesin equivalence ([BC, Proposition 3.6]): a pair (M, N) of infinite matroids satisfies the intersection property if and only if (M, N^*) has a packing/covering partition. Cited, not proved in the programme. The consequences in Section 3 of the fifth lesson (the pair (M_0, M_1) fails intersection, so the unrestricted infinite matroid intersection conjecture is false; Joo's Question 1.5) depend on it. Intended home: a lesson on infinite matroid duality and the Bowler-Carmesin equivalences.

Bowler-Carmesin equivalences of the separate Covering and Packing Conjectures with the packing/covering conjecture ([BC, Section 7]). Cited, not proved; the falsity of the separate conjectures stated in Section 3 of the fifth lesson depends on them.

Bruhn-Diestel-Kriesell-Pendavingh-Wollan: restrictions, duals and contractions of infinite matroids are matroids, and every spanning set contains a basis ([BDKPW, Sections 3-4]). Mentioned in the first lesson for context only; the proofs of the course do not use them.
